neighbours.label: position where a physical-activity verb such as 'walk' is the likely next word (able to / continue to / happy …)
fire: After months of physiotherapy she was finally able to walk without a cane.
Despite the pain in his knee he wanted to continue walking every morning.
The job involves bending, lifting and carrying boxes all day.
Thanks for reading, and until next time, happy hiking!
The puppy is now strong enough to run around the yard.
The doctor said he should keep walking at least a mile a day.
Workers must be capable of climbing ladders and lifting heavy loads.
Most toddlers learn to walk somewhere around their first birthday.
quiet: After months of physiotherapy she finally got a letter from the clinic.
Despite the pain in his knee he still enjoyed reading every morning.
The job involves filing, typing and answering phones all day.
Thanks for reading, and see you in next week's newsletter!
The puppy is now old enough to get its second vaccine.
The doctor said he should cut down on salt in his meals.
Workers must be familiar with the safety manual and the forms.
Most toddlers say their first word somewhere around their first birthday.
